Vikas, you asked why my feed is full of circuits. I'm Vijay, and last year I basically rebuilt my social media around robotics.
I unfollowed most of the random meme pages and followed science teachers, a couple of coding channels, and a woman in Pune who builds robots out of scrap. My feed went from noise to things I actually wanted to learn.
Then our school robotics club needed a way to show our work. I asked Mrs Kulkarni, our club teacher, if we could make a page. She said yes, with rules: no faces without permission, no school address, and she'd be an admin too. So we did.
We post one build every week. Last month a college robotics team commented on our line-follower and offered a video call to help with the sensor. We did the call in the lab, with Mrs Kulkarni there.
So my phone isn't just for scrolling now. It's a kind of second classroom.

qa.q: What rules did Mrs Kulkarni set for the page?
qa.a: No faces without permission, no school address, and she'd be an admin too.

qa.q: How does Vijay feel about social media now?
qa.a: Vijay feels excited and proud, seeing the phone as a second classroom rather than noise.

qa.q: What else could Vijay do to keep the feed useful?
qa.a: Every few months, unfollow accounts that drift back into noise and add ones tied to the next project.

qa.q: How might Mrs Kulkarni see the club page?
qa.a: Mrs Kulkarni likely feels pleased and reassured: the page shows students' work safely and has led to real help.

I'm Sahil, and Siddharth has been my deskmate since Class Six. For years his phone was all cricket memes. Then, around this summer, I noticed it change.
He started showing me posts from an astronomy teacher who explains the night sky every Friday, and a channel on basic coding for telescopes. He'd follow a scientist and then message me the best bits.
In September he asked Mr Rao if our science club could have its own page for the telescope photos we take on the terrace. Mr Rao agreed, as long as he checked every post first and nobody showed faces or the school's name. Siddharth made it that week.
Now the page has a few hundred followers, mostly other school clubs and some amateur astronomers. One of them, a retired teacher, sent the club a free star map, through Mr Rao.
I don't know if Siddharth planned all this. But his phone seems to be pointed somewhere now.

qa.q: What did the retired teacher send?
qa.a: A free star map, through Mr Rao.

qa.q: How might Siddharth feel about the science club page?
qa.a: Siddharth is probably proud and excited, seeing the page grow and bring real connections.

qa.q: What else could Siddharth do to build on this?
qa.a: Link up with other school clubs for a joint stargazing night, organised through Mr Rao.

qa.q: How does the change look to Sahil?
qa.a: Sahil sees the phone shift from memes to a real interest, though Sahil can't be sure Siddharth planned it.

grounding: A deskmate sees a student follow science teachers and coding channels and start a science club page with a teacher's approval, finding useful connections.
